primary_target: Dang et al. 2025 skull morphogenesis tissue model
scope: Source-constrained audit of Fisher–KPP branch selection, released model output, speed-estimator dependence, and alpha identifiability. Model results are not biological validation.

claims.exact_statement: Under a homogeneous A-homeostatic leading-edge reduction of the pinned coupled PDE, constant D, constant uniform drift removed, and source kD=alpha*(EB-EA)*phi, the osteoblast fraction obeys scalar Fisher-KPP logistic growth with r=(kB-kA)|rhoA_homeostasis + alpha*(EB-EA).
assumptions: Density is frozen at rhoA homeostasis in the leading edge.
Velocity is locally uniform and can be removed by a Galilean frame change.
The full source PDE's coupled density and force-balance dynamics are not represented by this scalar reduction.
claims.status: conditional_model_reduction_internally_derived; not a theorem for the full PDE or nature
claims.novelty_boundary: The Fisher-KPP reduction and speed-selection theory are established prior art; no novelty claim is made.

costs.source_access: Primary article, Supplementary Information, pinned simulator, and output matrices read locally.
costs.computation: Algebra plus sub-second NumPy replay; no PDE solver rerun or experimental acquisition.

claims.falsifier: The reduction is not an adequate leading-edge approximation if density, drift, or growth-rate coupling remains order-one across the observed leading-edge region.
claims.next_gate: Only compare with nature after independently measuring the live initial tail, leading-edge density, and cell/material-frame velocity.

claims.exact_statement: The pinned simulator's tanh initial phenotype profile has q0=2*aPhi/L=0.0053333 per micron. With its parameter row, the homogeneous scalar reduction gives qstar=0.0616367 per micron, c_shallow=10.7649 microns/hour, and c_pulled=1.8491 microns/hour. The released phi-half OLS trajectory is 21.7353 microns/hour; after subtracting the sampled model tissue velocity and adding the local density-gradient correction, the relative speed is 10.8082 microns/hour.
assumptions: The local reduction and its standard initial-tail branch apply to the scalar comparator only.
Source pressure parameters are interpreted in the simulator's converted units; no separate physical units for alpha are inferred.
The released matrices are analyzed as output; the Mathematica solver is not rerun.
claims.novelty_boundary: Branch selection is classical Fisher-KPP theory. The source-specific finding is only which branch the public simulator initializes and what its output yields under this definition.

costs.input_data: Pinned model output CSVs and parameter CSV, with local SHA-256 and Git blob verification in SOURCES.md.
costs.computation: Less than one second, Python/NumPy; no new hardware or wet-lab cost.

claims.falsifier: A replay under the source's exact published solver and a validated full-system convergence study could show that the scalar tail comparator does not explain the released simulation trajectory.
claims.next_gate: Re-run the exact nonlinear simulator with grid/time convergence and predeclared front definitions before using the prediction as more than a diagnostic.

claims.exact_statement: Within the scalar shallow-tail comparator, one adjusted wave speed c does not uniquely identify alpha if q is unknown: every q satisfying alpha(q)=[q(c-Dq)-delta_k]/delta_E>0 and q<sqrt((delta_k+alpha(q)*delta_E)/D) yields the same c. At c=10.8082254 microns/hour, q=0.0053333, 0.01, and 0.02 per micron yield alpha=3.5184e-6, 7.4452e-6, and 1.5685e-5 in simulator units, respectively, all with shallow-tail selection.
assumptions: D, deltaE, and delta_k are fixed to the source simulator values.
The adjusted speed is treated as a scalar-model target, not as a direct biological estimate.
claims.novelty_boundary: The algebra is elementary identifiability analysis, not a new theorem. Its value is blocking an unsupported one-speed inversion in this source interface.

costs.computation: Exact substitutions plus finite floating-point check.
missing_observations: an independent held-out wave speed after alpha fitting

claims.falsifier: The conditional nonidentifiability no longer applies if q is independently fixed and the scalar selection assumptions are validated.
claims.next_gate: Measure q and fit alpha on one condition, then test speed on a held-out condition.

claims.exact_statement: Three speed summaries from the released finite model output differ: interpolated phi=0.5 OLS gives 21.7353 microns/hour; the companion Rmd strict phi<0.5 origin fit gives 20.5881; the notebook two-window shift estimator gives 18.75. The notebook's absolute value encloses a signed spatial sum, so its residual 0.0372829 is not the L1 profile error; L1 at the same selected shift is 0.414950, and the L1 minimizer happens to retain that grid point in this replay.
assumptions: Index mapping, time window, and thresholds follow the pinned Rmd/notebook code.
These are model-output estimators, not competing natural measurements.
claims.status: source-code-and-output-replay; estimator dependence verified for one output; R time mapping checked with Rscript
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a scoped metric and estimator audit, not an allegation about the biological result or a complete code review.

costs.computation: Sub-second replay of two discrete time windows and 16 candidate shifts.

claims.falsifier: Different source outputs or a source-consistent L1 objective could remove the reported metric discrepancy; the speed-estimator spread still must be assessed with a declared estimand.
claims.next_gate: Make the intended speed estimand explicit and report a converged, window-stable estimate from the exact PDE solver.

claims.exact_statement: The released four ex-vivo interface data sets independently give 0-6 hour OLS slopes 12.1548, 10.8907, 15.0018, and 25.6663 microns/hour (mean 15.9284, sample SD 6.7157). The model phi-half OLS speed is within this across-data-set SD. Released tracked-cell front velocity summary is 13.1689±4.0948 microns/hour; it differs in observable from model Eulerian V.
assumptions: Source columns represent the Rmd times and interface heights.
The four data sets are treated as the across-series units; no hierarchical or embryo-level uncertainty model is fit.
claims.novelty_boundary: The measurements are source data. The within-SD comparison is descriptive, not a new biological finding.

costs.computation: One linear regression per data set; sub-second.

claims.falsifier: A different source-defined interface estimator or time window changes these slopes; report estimator sensitivity before using them as a validation target.
claims.next_gate: Compare a prefit model against held-out ex-vivo interface trajectories with a fixed front definition.

failures_and_unknowns.statement: The scalar KPP reduction is not the full source nonlinear moving-tissue PDE; density, flow, pressure and proliferation are dynamically coupled.

The biological initial exponent q, matched material-frame advection, held-out front speed, and BAPN live-speed response are unavailable in the reviewed source package; alpha and propagation law for nature remain UNKNOWN.

The published SI Fisher velocity equations and alpha inversion have a factor/sign/units concern under visual reading; an independent hostile auditor is checking this, so this report does not assert a corrected source verdict.
The 15-micron spatial grid cannot resolve the 16.2-micron scalar pulled-threshold length, and the exact PDE was not rerun or subjected to grid/time convergence checks.

Active migration, non-Fickian relative cell motion, contact-age kinetics and mechanical relay remain equally informed alternatives to a scalar propagation interpretation; the primary source acknowledges migration versus displacement limitations.
